proposals.risk: a result its requirement or criteria name is computed or chosen wrongly
proposals.rationale: When all automatic credentials are blocked, the earliest-wait selection picks the credentials with the longest wait (max) instead of the shortest, so the chosen key is wrongly computed.

proposals.risk: a result its requirement or criteria name is computed or chosen wrongly
proposals.rationale: Key availability preference is dropped when selecting available credentials: only the first available key is considered blocked-aware via a wait computed for the wrong key, so the reported wait comes from a stale first candidate and rotation among available keys is broken (preferred set restricted to the single lowest key id).

proposals.risk: an external interaction its requirement rules out happens anyway
proposals.rationale: Availability preference is only applied when more than one key is available; with exactly one available key among blocked ones, the key manager rotates over all keys and may pick a blocked key, causing a blocked credential to be used (and waited on/called) while an available one exists.

proposals.risk: an external interaction its requirement rules out happens anyway
proposals.rationale: Limiter wait is only reported for automatic key selection; for explicitly pinned keys the wait is reported as 0.0, so a blocked route looks available and is called instead of being skipped or failing fast.

proposals.risk: an error the interface must report comes out with the wrong type or status, or not at all
proposals.rationale: Unknown-provider error is raised with the wrong exception type (TypeError instead of ValueError), so callers handling the documented ValueError miss it.

proposals.risk: an error the interface must report comes out with the wrong type or status, or not at all
proposals.rationale: When every automatic credential is blocked, the earliest-available key is chosen but the returned wait is reported as 0, so the blocked state is never surfaced and the caller neither fails fast nor waits; the blocked route is called anyway.
